bibl.note: One-based viewer images 178–179; printed page numbers are 44 lower. Archive page labels differ from both. The actual images, rather than another witness or uncorrected OCR, supply the readings.

normalization.p: Source spelling, capitalization, punctuation, written ampersands and visible accents are retained. Long s and typographic ligatures are represented by standard s and constituent letters. Letter spacing in display capitals and quotation glyph shapes may be represented schematically. No modern-edition readings are substituted.

segmentation.p: Each l represents one canonical verse, with stable numbering and a link to its existing image region. Source verse order and headings are retained. Couplet grouping and canonical line numbers are editorial. A displaced word may remain within its verse with its position marked.

Full-page line starts were independently checked on every page. Even lines have the visible ordinary inset. Verse 2 has an additional three-character approximation of the space beside the two-line opening capital; it is not inferred from verse parity.

correction.p: Uncertain readings remain locally marked with unclear or gap. Observations and uncertainties are documented for a different source reader; ink colour alone does not establish erasure or a separate hand.

revisionDesc.change: First reader inspected and transcribed all 46 verses from the source images; independent source review pending.

Independent reviewer inspected all 46 extant verses against full-page source images and enlarged bands; corrected supported readings, punctuation and accents; checked line starts and all source notes; original annotation rectangles preserved.
Independent opening-crop follow-up confirmed the second letter after the large initial is uppercase: Nox corrected to source NOx; remaining opening letters and extra verse-2 space rechecked.

Fresh corpus source reading rechecked all 46 verses, every evidence note, headings, page furniture and full-page line starts. No further verse wording changes were supported. Prior independent second-pass history is retained; changed readings were additionally corroborated from native crops by /root/w_review_c. See W-3.5-second-pass.md.

lg.label: Elegia V. Somnium, Elegia quae ex MSS. huc revocata est.
lg.l: NOx erat: & somnus lassos submisit ocellos.
Terruerunt animum talia visa meum.
Colle sub aprico celeberrimus ilice lucus
Stabat; & in ramis multa latebat avis.
Area gramineo suberat viridissima prato,
Uvida de guttis lene sonantis aquae.
Ipse sub arboreis vitabam frondibus aestum;
Fronde sub arboreâ sed tamen aestus erat.
Ecce, petens variis immixtas floribus herbas,
Constitit ante oculos candida vacca meos.
Candidior nivibus, tunc cum cecidere recentes;
In liquidas nondum quas mora vertit aquas.
Candidior, quod adhuc spumis stridentibus albet,
Et modo siccatam, lacte, reliquit ovem.
Taurus erat comes huic, feliciter ille maritus:
Cumque suâ teneram conjuge pressit humum.
Dum jacet, & lentè revocatas ruminat herbas,
Atque iterum pasto pascitur ante cibo;
Visus erat, somno vires adimente; ferenti
Cornigerum terrae deposuisse caput.
Huc levibus cornix pennis delapsa per auras
Venit; & in viridi garrula sedit humo.
Terque bovis niveae petulanti pectora rostro
Fodit; & albentes abstulit ore jubas.
Illa locum taurumque diu cunctata relinquit.
Sed niger in vaccae pectore livor erat.
Utque procul vidit carpentes pabula tauros;
(Carpebant tauri pabula laeta procul)
Illuc se rapuit, gregibusque immiscuit illis;
Et petiit herbae fertilioris humum.
Dic, age, nocturnae, quicumque es, imaginis augur,
(Si quid habent veri) visa quid ista ferant.
Sic ego: nocturnae sic dixit imaginis augur,
Expendens animo singula visa suo:
Quem tu mobilibus foliis vitare volebas,
Sed male vitabas, aestus amoris erat.
Vacca puella tua est. aptus color ille puellae.
Tu vir, & in vaccâ compare taurus eras.
Pectora quod rostro cornix fodiebat acuto;
Ingenium dominae lena movebit anus.
Quod cunctata diu taurum sua vacca reliquit;
Frigidus in viduo destituere toro.
Livor, & adverso maculae sub pectore nigrae,
Pectus adulterii labe carere negant.
Dixerat interpres. gelido mihi sanguis ab ore
Fugit; & ante oculos nox stetit alta meos.

div.note: The printed poem heading is present above this witness text and is transcribed separately in heading metadata.
The two-line opening capital displaces verse 2 farther right than the ordinary inset. An additional horizontal space of three characters approximates this observed layout.
